text:
QUOTE: "It then calls `client.createPost` again with the same content. On success it writes the server's post to the database and updates the channel's last-post time, unless the post is a CRT reply. - On failure it sets `failed: true` again, or deletes the post if the error is one of the three removal errors above. It does not retry on its own."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says retryFailedPost makes a single new createPost call with no retry of its own (and noRetry/retryLimit 0), and on failure re-marks the post failed or deletes it for the same three errors.
